A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MPRT research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and complete enough for reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 report original simulated error rates, PC causal-discovery results, and discovered structures from Big Five personality data.

after.justification: The original simulations and personality-data analyses are retained, with an additional KCI comparison reported in Table 1.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same correlation estimator, matrix parameterization, CCA statistic, and permutation procedure. Corrected cross-references and the SVD sign convention introduced in the proof do not establish a changed rank-test procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic continuous and mixed-data rank testing, synthetic PC graph recovery, and the same Big Five openness/neuroticism application. The added comparator uses existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds KCI to the PC-algorithm comparison, retaining Fisher-Z, CCART-D, and CCART-DE. The comparator sets in the other experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated sample sizes, discretization thresholds, three-category construction, error-rate evaluation, and skeleton F1/SHD metrics are unchanged. KCI is added under the existing Table 1 conditions without a separately documented protocol revision.

E4.justification: The sample-size analyses in Figures 2–3 and personality case study in Figure 4 are retained. No new ablation, sensitivity test, robustness experiment, or error analysis appears; the non-Gaussian discussion remains conceptual.

E5.justification: Both versions report 3,000 random trials and 200 MPRT permutations in Section 4.1. There is no added seed information, uncertainty reporting, or between-method significance testing.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds KCI F1 scores of 0.81, 0.88, and 0.86 and SHD values of 1.00, 0.80, and 0.93 for N = 500, 1000, and 2000. Existing table values and plotted results are unchanged, and MPRT retains the best reported F1 and SHD.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 substantially revises Theorem 4's proof, adding pseudo-likelihood consistency, SVD continuity, sign fixing, and a continuous-mapping argument for estimated canonical projections. It newly assumes distinct population singular values, restricting the argument although the theorem statement remains unchanged. The other proofs and definitions are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same novelty, discretization coverage, exchangeability, error-control, and causal-discovery claims. The conclusion is shortened, but its omitted error-control statement remains a central claim elsewhere.

C2.justification: The non-Gaussian discussion moves from v1 Appendix C.2 to v2 Section 4.5, with a substantive qualification: recovery without a known distributional form changes from a problem that 'cannot be solved' to one that 'may be very hard.' The revised passage also mentions recovering thresholds alongside correlations.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a specific repository address for the planned code release, whereas v1 only promises future code availability. Both describe availability prospectively; the PDFs do not establish that code has been released.

R1.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendix A.1 add references supporting likelihood estimation and SVD arguments. Appendix D adds Sun et al. (2025a,b), discussing discretization-aware partial-correlation tests and a method-of-moments approach. These are limited extensions of the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: Localized edits expand Section 4.5, move the non-Gaussian discussion into the main text, renumber the remaining appendix discussion, correct cross-references, and shorten the conclusion. Affiliations and publication information are updated and acknowledgments added; the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a KCI row, and appendix Figures 5 and 6 are regrouped on one page. Text and equations reflow around these changes, but all six figures retain their graphical content and captions.

improvement.justification: The KCI comparison, code-location information, and editorial clarifications provide limited benefits. However, v1's short Theorem 4 proof is replaced by an argument assuming distinct singular values, while the unchanged rank-null permits repeated zero singular values when K-k exceeds one. The PDFs do not reconcile this restriction with the theorem's general statement. The expanded proof therefore has an unresolved central limitation, making the net quality effect of the revision unclear.
